findings.claim: That guidance implies free cash flow of roughly USD 12bn against adjusted EBITDA of roughly USD 6bn — free cash flow at approximately twice EBITDA. In a capital equipment business that is only possible through large customer advance payments on a rapidly growing order book.

risks.text: Reported free cash flow is running at roughly twice EBITDA on customer advances. This flatters the cash figure the market is capitalising and reverses when order growth slows.
Consolidated margin guidance was not raised alongside revenue and free cash flow, so group profitability is improving more slowly than the headline suggests.
Backlog cancellation terms are undisclosed, so the firmness of USD 176bn cannot be assessed.

catalysts.text: Q3 2026 results — whether the FCF-to-EBITDA gap persists or narrows

conclusions: The demand is genuine and unusually well contracted for this protocol: USD 176bn of backlog, orders up 88% organically, and a demand driver — data centre load and grid replacement — that is physical rather than narrative.

The critical finding is in the guidance structure. Free cash flow guidance was raised from USD 6.5-7.5bn to USD 11.5-12.5bn while adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was left unchanged at 12-14%. That is free cash flow at roughly twice EBITDA.

In a capital equipment business, free cash flow at twice EBITDA comes from customer advance payments on a rapidly growing order book. Those are deposits on equipment not yet built — a liability, not earnings — and they reverse as the backlog converts or if order growth slows.
Group profitability is improving more slowly than the top line: revenue guidance was raised, margin guidance was not.
Applying the classification test, the demand is well contracted. What is speculative is not the orders but whether the scarcity pricing survives the capacity build.
thesisImpact: Phase 3 identifies what the market is actually capitalising. On a reported free cash flow of USD 12bn the equity looks reasonably priced; on underlying earnings of roughly USD 6bn of EBITDA and USD 0.6bn of quarterly net income it does not. Phase 5 must model underlying cash generation rather than the advance-inflated reported figure, and must say so.
